title: Answer: no account of consciousness, which enters only as a question of scale

statements.text: Causal emergence takes no position on what consciousness is. It enters as a question of scale: causal emergence might explain the spatiotemporal scale of consciousness in the brain, and in integrated information theory that scale is fixed by where integrated information peaks. Hoel keeps that analysis apart from his own: justifying the uniform distribution of interventions through the intrinsic perspective of integrated information theory relies on accepting that theory's postulates, including its analysis of consciousness.
statements.scope: Causal emergence is widespread across measures of causation (2022), Can the macro beat the micro (2016) and Causal emergence 2.0 (2025)
